## What the chronicles say [Record]

[Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd) was baptised in the Catholic rite at Tapiau (Tepliava) on 21 October 1383 and took the name Wigand. The Order and Jogaila's alliance (the Treaty of Dubysa of 31 October 1382) collapsed in June 1383, and in early September the Knights and Vytautas briefly took Trakai and unsuccessfully attacked Vilnius. Konrad Zöllner von Rotenstein had been elected Grand Master after Kniprode's death on 24 June 1382. The date is attested in the Order's records (the chronicler is not identified in my sources; verify). The Königsberg treaty followed on 30 January 1384.

## What really happened [Saga]

A lying baptism. Vytautas kneels before the bishop of Sambia in a chapel full of incense that smells of cellars; every "Amen" is a nail driven into his ancestors. The stained glass cracks at the promise: Perkūnas's warning. His amber pebble dies, cold, a plain stone: the lie breaks the connection to the elements, and the baptismal font is a consecrated place (magic §5.4). He receives the Order's sword. [Henė](../characters/hanulas.qmd) is among the knights in German furs.

## Consequences

Caused by [the audience at Marienburg](ev_marienburg_audience.qmd), which follows [the Dykra rescue](ev_dykra_rescue.qmd) and [the refuge in Masovia](ev_masovia_refuge.qmd). It leads to [the Treaty of Königsberg](ev_konigsberg.qmd).

## Dramatisation

Book I ch. 18 "Geležinis Magistras" (Vytautas; winter 1382–83, Marienburg) and ch. 19 "Velnio Sandėris" (Vytautas; the text jumps the winter, spring and summer to 21 October 1383, Tepliava chapel).
